J1_line_asserts_challenged_proposition.justification: The response challenges 'If G is a diamond-free graph, then its block graph B(G) is triangle-free.' First-choice line 127 is the body of Proposition BlockTF: 'Let $G$ be a $\kk$-free graph. Then $B(G)\in\tf$.' Both symbols are fixed inside the packet: line 45 defines $\tf$ as 'the family of all triangle-free graphs', line 47 says 'we refer to the graph on four vertices with five edges as $\kk$' (K_4 minus an edge, the diamond, spelled out again at line 98 as a,b,c,d with ab,ac,ad,bc,bd edges and cd a non-edge), and line 123 defines B(G) for a $\kk$-free G. So line 127 states exactly the implication attacked, and states it under $\kk$-freeness alone - no claw-freeness, no connectedness, no finiteness - while the neighbouring statements carry their own hypotheses (line 103 assumes G in $\ltf$, lines 85/120/123 assume $\kk$-free), so no ambient claw-free convention is in force. Both readers graded YES and I agree.

J2_evidence_specified.justification: One named finite witness with the hypothesis check and the computed conclusion: 'The star graph K_{1,3} is diamond-free (K_4-e-free), but its block graph B(K_{1,3}) is K_3, which contains a triangle.' The graph, the property it has, and the value of B on it are all given; nothing was left for the verifier to supply, notwithstanding that the attempt is recorded as ending by budget exhaustion.

J3_evidence_check.justification: Exact finite computation of exactly the supplied witness in readings/ADJ/scripts/P06_check.py, implemented from the source's own definitions and nothing else. (i) K_{1,3} has three edges, so no four of its vertices carry five edges: it is $\kk$-free (my script also confirms it is K_4-free, so the witness survives even a misreading of $\kk$ as K_4). (ii) By line 85 ('$e\sim e'$ if the endpoints of $e,e'$ span a clique in $G$') the three edges lie in three distinct classes, since ab ~ ac would require the absent edge bc. (iii) Reading the classes as vertex sets - the source's own reading at line 85 ('two distinct classes are either disjoint or have exactly one vertex in common'), line 88 and line 130 ('there exist distinct vertices $v_{xy}\in\cls x\cap\cls y$') - the classes {a,b}, {a,c}, {a,d} pairwise meet in the centre a, so line 123's definition makes B(K_{1,3}) the complete graph on three vertices, which contains a triangle and is not in $\tf$. Hypothesis satisfied, conclusion false: the witness refutes line 127 as written. The same computation locates the gap in the source's own proof at line 130, which needs the three intersection vertices to be distinct while here they all coincide - i.e. the missing hypothesis is claw-freeness, which line 127 does not state. Control cases in the script (K_3, P_4, both in the paper's intended class) give block graphs with no triangle, so the implementation is not manufacturing triangles.

J4_consequence_overreach.justification: The saved response is the emitted JSON alone - the ranked labels 127, 126, 130, one claim sentence and one counterexample sentence - with no trace and no stated consequence. It does not assert that Proposition TFBlock at lines 133-134, the remark at line 148 or the paper's main results fail, so there is nothing that could overreach.

notes: I reproduced the computation independently before reading either reader and reach the same values; all three readings agree on all four judgments. Two things a joint view should carry. (1) The one interpretive choice is whether the intersection in line 123 is of classes as vertex sets or as edge sets; under the edge-set reading distinct classes are always disjoint, B(G) would be edgeless and line 127 vacuously true, so the witness depends on the vertex-set reading - which is the source's own, used in its statements at lines 85 and 90 and in its proof at line 130. (2) This packet is in the adjudication set because the record is flagged as ending by budget exhaustion, not because the readers disagreed; see the disposition for how I treat that.

adjudication.reason: Both readers agree on every judgment and my independent computation reproduces theirs: the claw satisfies line 127's only hypothesis and its block graph, built strictly from the source's own definitions, is K_3, so the proposition is false as written and the source's proof at line 130 breaks exactly where the missing claw-freeness would have been used. This is mathematically the strongest objection in the set I adjudicated, and it is aimed at precisely what the selected line says. The question the packet was sent for is the budget-exhaustion flag, and I resolve it this way: the flag is a property of the generation record, but the emitted answer is a syntactically complete JSON whose candidate list, claim and witness are all present, and the refutation uses nothing that could have been cut off - so the incompleteness does not degrade what the response supplied, and grading it PROTOCOL_INVALID_ATTEMPT would discard a complete, verified objection on a records technicality. I therefore record VALID_ALTERNATIVE_OBJECTION, and flag that if the analysis excludes budget-exhausted attempts as a class, this packet must be moved to that cell by that rule rather than on any assessment of its content, and the exclusion must then be applied uniformly to every such record in the sample.
adjudication.scale_note: Disposition vocabulary applied blind to the gold label: VALID_ALTERNATIVE_OBJECTION = valid evidence with J1 = YES; VALID_EVIDENCE_BUT_LINE_MISMATCH = valid evidence with J1 not YES; PROTOCOL_INVALID_ATTEMPT reserved for attempts whose supplied evidence is itself incomplete.
